Body parser middlewares: json(), urlencoded(), text(), raw(), xml()

All parsers read the full request body into memory before processing. Streaming body parsing is not supported. For large file uploads, use the multipart parser's maxFileSize limit to prevent out-of-memory conditions.

Returns the default options for the JSON body parser.Returns the default options for the text body parser.Returns the default options for the raw body parser.Returns the default options for the urlencoded body parser.Returns the default options for the XML body parser.Extracts the lowercased charset parameter from a Content-Type header value, or an empty string if absent.Parses the body as JSON only when the request carries a JSON Content-Type. Requests without a Content-Type (or with a non-matching one) pass through to next() with the body left unprocessed.Parses the body as text when the Content-Type matches, storing it in the body_text request local.Parses the body as raw bytes when the Content-Type matches, storing it in the body_raw request local.Parses a urlencoded form body, storing each decoded field in a form_-prefixed request local.Parses the body as XML text when the Content-Type matches, storing it in the body_xml request local.Middleware that auto-detects JSON or urlencoded bodies and runs the matching parser before calling next.Synchronous variant of bodyParser. Supports JSON and urlencoded parsing only (no text/raw/xml). Kept inline for the sync hot path; if parsing behavior changes, update both this and the async json()/urlencoded() middlewares.

Reads the request body as raw bytes and stores it in req.locals["body_raw"]. Nim strings can hold arbitrary binary data (they are length-delimited, not null-terminated like C strings), so this works correctly for binary content.
